business_problem: Morningstar needed to leave its data centers, modernize a self-hosted MongoDB-backed web service into a reusable API platform, and give investment customers faster, more personalized access to large volumes of market and portfolio data.
solution_summary: Morningstar used MongoDB Atlas as a key part of its broader cloud modernization so investment data, ratings, and portfolio insights could move from on-premises and server-rendered delivery into cloud-native API services. As the company worked to exit its data centers, teams broke down monoliths, adopted serverless patterns where appropriate, and reimagined Direct Web Services from an embedded ASP.NET iframe model into Dynamic Service APIs running on a multi-region Atlas deployment. Atlas pulls disparate data from many backend sources into collections that can be optimized for specific product use cases, making it easier to expose personalized investor dashboards without forcing customers to host heavy infrastructure themselves. Morningstar has since expanded Atlas into newer strategic platforms, including Morningstar Wealth Platform for financial advisors, and is preparing Atlas Search for text matching without adding separate ETL-heavy search systems.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Hosts Morningstar's multi-region API and product databases after the company's move away from self-managed and on-premises infrastructure.

data_flow: Data from Morningstar's backend research and portfolio systems is collected into MongoDB Atlas collections, API services query those collections to deliver personalized investor dashboards and advisor experiences, and future text search will run on the same Atlas data foundation.
business_outcome: Morningstar moved closer to customers with lower-latency infrastructure, accelerated product development for reusable APIs, and created a simpler path for investment clients and financial advisors to consume personalized data services.
metrics: Morningstar provides investment data, analytics, and research on more than 600,000 investment offerings.
The company manages $260 billion in assets.
Morningstar Wealth Platform is used by more than 255,000 financial advisors all over the world.
